sentences.text:
---- Respondent
For Appellant/State : Shri Anand Verma, Dy. Govt. Advocate For Respondent : None Hon'ble Shri
Justice Sanjay Kumar Jaiswal Judgment On Board 14/12/2023

1. This acquittal appeal under section 378(3) CrPC has been preferred by the State against the
judgment of acquittal dated 15.03.2011 passed by the learned Special Judge (Sc & St Act), Durg,
Chhattisgarh, in Special Case No. 24/2009 whereby the respondent herein has been acquitted of the
charge under Section 376(1) of Ipc read with Section 3(2)(v) of the Sc & St (Prevention of Atrocity)
Act, 1989.

2. The case of prosecution, in brief, is that the prosecutrix Pw-2 is the resident of village Bagheli,
P.S. Arjunda, District Durg.
She was working as a cook in Primary School, Bagheli, and was preparing mid- day-meals for the children.
The respondent/accused was also working in the said school as a Teacher.

On the date of incident i.e. 20.03.2009 at about 11 a.m., after mid-day-meal,
when the prosecutrix went to Kitchen to keep the utensils, the accused came there and asked her Neutral Citation 2023:CGHC:32619 for keys which she gave him.
Thereafter, the accused asked for photo and handkerchief to which she said that the same was not there.
On this, the accused forcefully caught the prosecutrix, threw her on the ground and committed sexual intercourse with her.
When the prosecutrix tried to shout, he threatened her.
The prosecutrix firstly did not tell anyone about the incident due to fear of public shame but on 24.03.2009 she told Sarpanch Sukhitram Sahu about the incident.
Thereafter, she went to Arjunda Police Station and made a report of the incident.

3. After appreciating oral as well as documentary evidence, the learned trial Court found that the prosecution has failed to prove its case beyond reasonable doubt and vide impugned judgment dated State Of Chhattigarh vs Vijay Kumar on 14 December, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/100648758/
1 15.03.2011, acquitted the accused/respondent of the aforesaid charges.

entities.text: State Of Chhattigarh vs Vijay Kumar
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Hence, this appeal.

4. Learned counsel appearing for the State/appellant submits that the trial Court has erred in disbelieving the statement of the prosecutrix PW-2 in which she has categorically stated regarding the commission of offence.

It is submitted that the prosecutrix in her statement has stated that she had disclosed the incident to the Sarpanch on the same day, but the trial Court while passing the impugned judgment has overlooked this fact.

It is argued that the case of prosecution is fully established against the accused beyond reasonable doubt, therefore, the impugned judgment is contrary to law facts and circumstances of the case and the same is liable to be set aside and the respondent deserves to be convicted and sentenced for the said offence.
Neutral Citation 2023:CGHC:32619 5.
No one appeared on behalf of accused/respondent in final hearing.

6. Heard learned counsel for the State and perused the materials available on record including the impugned judgment.
7.
It is an undisputed fact that both the parties were familiar with each other before the date of incident.
At the time of incident, the prosecutrix was a married lady aged about 35 years.
She was working as a Cook for preparation of Mid-day-mill in Primary School, Bagheli where the accused was also working as a Teacher.
The incident is said to have happened on 20.03.2009.

The prosecutrix has stated that at the time of commission of offence she did not shout nor did she tell anyone in the school about the incident and after 4 days of the incident, on 24.03.2009 she lodged a report.
In cross-examination she has admitted that the accused had only caught hold her hand and did not do anything with her.

She has clearly admitted that she had lodged the report after much consideration so that she would not be removed from the job because there was talk of removing her from the job on the basis that her work was not satisfied.
8. The prosecutrix has stated that the accused had committed rape on her.
But, in her cross-examination she has admitted that the accused had only caught hold her hand and did not do anything with her.
The prosecutrix did not tell anything to anyone immediately after the incident instead she remained silent for four days.

She had told her husband about the incident on the same day but the prosecution did not examine her husband which shows that she had consented to whatever happened with her and that is why the prosecution did not examine her husband.
Neutral Citation 2023:CGHC:32619 9.

All these facts that the prosecutrix was a married lady and her not showing any resistance when the accused had sexual intercourse with her, having sexual intercourse with the accused silently in the school kitchen and not making any noise, maintaining silence for four days continuously, not supporting by her husband in lodging the report despite telling him about the incident on the same day, compel to come to the conclusion that the accused had sexual intercourse with the prosecutrix only with her consent or else the accused only caught hold her hand and nothing was done to her, or State Of Chhattigarh vs Vijay Kumar on 14 December, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/100648758/
2 else, the prosecutrix had lodged the report so that she would not be removed from the job.

entities.text: State Of Chhattigarh vs Vijay Kumar
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Therefore, the offense charged against the accused is not proved beyond reasonable doubt.

10. Hon'ble Supreme Court in the matter of Muralidhar @ Gidda & Another vs. State of Karnataka,
reported in (2014) 5 SCC 730, has held that if two views are possible, the appellate Court should not interfere with the judgment of acquittal, even otherwise, the prosecution in the present case has utterly failed in proving its case beyond reasonable doubt.

entities.text:
Muralidhar @ Gidda & Another vs. State of Karnataka,
reported in (2014) 5 SCC 730
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
11. Having gone through the evidence available on record, keeping in view the settled legal position regarding the scope of interference in the appeals against acquittal, this Court finds no such illegality or infirmity in the impugned judgment of the trial Court acquitting the respondent of the charge under Section 376(1) of IPC read with Section 3(2)(v) of the SC & ST (Prevention of Atrocity)
Act, 1989.
The said finding is based on the proper appreciation of overall evidence available on record.

It is trite law that if two views are possible in the Neutral Citation 2023:CGHC:32619 given set of evidence, the appellate Court should not ordinarily interfere with the judgment of acquittal until and unless the said finding is found to have been arrived at by ignoring relevant facts and considering the irrelevant ones.
However, no such illegality is noticed in the impugned judgment warranting interference by this Court.
12. Thus, the instant acquittal appeal being devoid of substance deserves to be and is accordingly dismissed.

Sd/-
(Sanjay Kumar Jaiswal) JUDGE Khatai State Of Chhattigarh vs Vijay Kumar on 14 December, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/100648758/
